criterionTransfers.text: - [ ] Compare existing email and Teams capabilities against current licence, connector policy, permissions, delivery audience and connection ownership; flag prerequisites before configuring.

- [ ] Agree an event/channel/recipient matrix, starting with request received and answered. Consider availability cancellation and exceptional failure alerts explicitly; do not silently add every draft event to MVP.
- [ ] Distinguish direct notifications from channel announcements; avoid exposing candidate/comments/request details to unrelated channel members.
- [ ] Evaluate how recipients notice and open a request, including a link into the app, without routine organiser emails.
- [ ] Allow necessary exceptional admin support, but avoid per-user notification grants or manual routine dispatch.
- [ ] Agree retry/deduplication and failure reporting; notification failure does not undo request/membership business state.
- [ ] Record the selected MVP events/channels and deferred events before #21 implementation. If no existing permitted option fits, report the constraint; no trial, premium upgrade or paid workaround.
- [ ] Inspect the actual old workbook only when this phase starts; no guessed columns, colour-based statuses, memberships or culture mappings.
- [ ] Document source-to-target field mapping and unresolved rows/colours with the owner; distinguish language/culture sharing from interest.
- [ ] Resolve identities against company accounts without replacing the unique Person identity with a participant-editable email.
- [ ] Dry-run duplicate/missing-data validation and produce an exception report; do not silently drop rows or guess values.
- [ ] Recreate confirmed existing groups/memberships with approved capacities and free slots; unresolved cases are explicit exceptions.
- [ ] Keep migration confirmation independent of participation and validation status; decide whether unconfirmed profiles are discoverable.
- [ ] Use supported existing Microsoft tools; flag any setup/licence prerequisite. One-off human mapping review is allowed; no ongoing Forms-to-list duplication.
- [ ] Make reruns safe and reconcile source/target counts and samples before release.
- [ ] Record participant review/invitation handling only after notification options are agreed; preserve originals and document recovery.
- [ ] Verify an approach supported by existing SharePoint/Power Automate entitlement and configuration; flag prerequisites first. No paid lock service or external backend.
- [ ] Revalidate caller authority, participant availability, group Open state and capacity at acceptance time.
- [ ] Repeated acceptance/retry creates one logical result, no duplicate group/membership or duplicate event notifications.
- [ ] Two acceptances for the last slot cannot both succeed. Test person-to-person creation and joins, including concurrent runs from different flows.
- [ ] Persist enough operation state to recover partial request/group/membership writes safely; no false Accepted result when required writes fail.
- [ ] Reconcile free slots from authoritative memberships; a transient failure must not create hidden extra capacity or delete history.
- [ ] Test two members responding to the same group join request, sender cancel versus accept races, and retries after partial failure. One terminal decision and one logical membership result.
- [ ] Ordinary successful acceptance is automatic; exceptional recovery may be handled by admins with a clear record.
- [ ] Record tenant evidence and integrate into #11/#12/#17 tests before those acceptance paths close.
- [x] PR #59 merged and #46 closed; target contract accepted.
- [ ] Identify organiser contact route before publishing private-contact guidance. This decision is tracked here rather than blocking the field contract; no email/address is guessed.
- [x] PR #51 documents the reviewed contract and stable test catalogue; not deployment.
- [x] #46 contract accepted; follow-ups belong to receiving implementation tickets.
- [ ] Finish #5 culture/optional-time-zone registration and tenant tests (merged partial preparation PR #52), then #6 independent participation/openness.
- [ ] Extend/integrate #7/#9 participant compatibility; prepare #12/#13 structures before #16 group discovery.
- [ ] Deliver #10/#11/#17 and #12 accepted memberships with #47 retry/concurrency safeguards.
- [ ] Complete #14 leaving and relevant access/authorization safeguards.
- [ ] Decide #49 then implement/test selected #21 notifications.
- [ ] Record relevant #25–#28 acceptance/scale/handover evidence; then #48 actual Excel mapping/import last.
- [ ] Verify ordinary-user access and remaining release gates before wider rollout.
- [ ] Flag all required permissions/settings/connections/licences to the owner and verify before building this data-access path.
- [ ] Implement approved #46 profile/group fields with #7/#16; exclude email/raw identity/admin/system fields; no directory or Comments notice.
- [ ] Blank optional Time zone does not exclude a compatible candidate.
- [ ] Retrieve candidates through the authenticated, authorized path without giving users general read access to Participants.
- [ ] Reuse compatible eligibility from #7/#9; ranking #8 remains Later and is not a dependency; this ticket covers secure access and integration, not a second matching implementation.
- [ ] Direct invocation or tampered identity/query/record inputs cannot bypass eligibility or reveal all profiles.
- [ ] Candidate presentation is read-only and requires no per-search approval, manual matching or per-candidate permission grant.
- [ ] Verify discovery with two normal accounts while own-profile access stays protected.
- [ ] Update discovery/setup documentation and record evidence before discovery rollout.
- [ ] POC-18B passed; flag and verify any new permission, licence, connection or configuration prerequisite before implementation.
- [ ] Preserve existing records and unique Participant account. Registration opens/creates/updates only the authenticated user's profile.
- [ ] Protect the underlying data as proven, including inherited and existing item access; hiding app controls alone is insufficient.

- [ ] Retest the implemented current registration contract: save/reopen, multiple language/culture lookups, language-only/culture-only/share-only participation and optional blank/cleared Time zone. Preserve later participation/openness choices if #6 has been delivered.
- [ ] Reject attempts to change another user's record, identity or managed fields; handle duplicate creates and update conflicts.
- [ ] Verify two ordinary accounts plus admin, including direct SharePoint/API access and published-app access.
- [ ] New users join and maintain profiles without routine admin approvals, individual sharing/grants or manual group maintenance.
- [ ] Record one-time cutover steps and operational dependencies upfront; preserve data and document recovery without restoring broad exposure.
- [ ] Update setup instructions, design, plan and acceptance evidence in the implementation PR.
- [ ] POC-18A is complete; all required permissions, settings, licences and connections were flagged to the owner and verified before this proof starts.
- [ ] Use an isolated test app/list or equivalent, with no changes to the working registration app.
- [ ] Authenticate the caller through the selected supported method; do not trust an app-supplied email, identity or record ID as authorization.
- [ ] A can create, reopen and update only A's record; B can do the same for B.
- [ ] Direct list/item/API access and tampered requests cannot read or modify the other user's record.
- [ ] Administrators retain access; normal users do not gain flow ownership or access to other users' execution data.
- [ ] Both users self-onboard without individual admin approvals, grants or manual participant/group management.
- [ ] Record evidence, outstanding limits and a proceed/stop decision. A failed prerequisite must not trigger a new configuration workaround without notifying the owner first.
- [ ] Record current app/list/flow permissions and available connectors without changing the working app or accessing other participants' data.
- [ ] List every required permission, tenant setting, connection, licence, sharing configuration and one-time setup step. Mark each verified, unavailable or unknown, with evidence.
- [ ] Notify the owner of every prerequisite and verify it before relying on it. An unknown prerequisite blocks dependent implementation.
- [ ] Compare feasible approaches retaining unique Participant account. Flow-mediated access is only an option, not the selected solution.

- [ ] Demonstrate ordinary registration, updates, joining and future discovery without routine admin approvals, per-person grants or manual participant/group maintenance. Necessary critical-case admin support is allowed.
- [ ] Distinguish one-time setup from recurring operational maintenance; flag ownership/credential/permission dependencies explicitly.
- [ ] Record the chosen approach and its limits in docs/POC_18_PARTICIPANT_ACCESS.md. If none meets the requirements, report the constraint before building a workaround.
- [ ] Admin can identify participants available/waiting for connections.
- [ ] Admin can identify active groups.
- [ ] Admin can identify Closed groups under Open/Closed/Ended; participant Paused is a separate status.
- [ ] Admin can identify groups needing members.
- [ ] Admin can identify ended groups.
- [ ] Admin can identify stale participants/groups.
- [ ] Admin can identify records requiring intervention.
- [ ] Admin can perform agreed status overrides or corrections.
- [ ] Scheduled check identifies stale records.
- [ ] Appropriate participant/group member receives reminder.
- [ ] Failure to send reminder is observable.
- [ ] Reminder does not automatically end a group.
- [ ] LastConfirmedAt or equivalent freshness data exists.
- [ ] Stale participants can be identified.
- [ ] Stale groups can be identified.
- [ ] Records are not automatically deleted because they become stale.
- [ ] Another admin/developer can follow repository instructions.

- [ ] Another permitted owner can reproduce documented one-time manual list/column/index setup, app/flow configuration and optional local validation. Automated tenant provisioning is not required or claimed.
- [ ] No local-only secret/configuration is required.
- [ ] Failures produce understandable diagnostic output.
- [ ] Permissions, settings, connectors, existing entitlements, ownership and exceptional recovery are explicit and verified before relying on them. Ordinary use needs no routine admin actions.
- [ ] Handover distinguishes desired schema from confirmed live settings and records test IDs, deployed versions and actual acceptance evidence.
- [ ] Discovery tested at approximately 200 participants.
- [ ] Discovery tested at approximately 1,000 participants.
- [ ] Discovery tested at approximately 5,000 participants.
- [ ] Query latency is recorded.
- [ ] Power Apps delegation warnings/limitations are recorded.
- [ ] Any client-side large-data processing is identified.

- [ ] Document supported-platform query/pagination/bounds limits and feasible optimizations within existing entitlements. No hosted service, paid API, premium connector or new runtime is an approved fallback.
- [ ] Verify test setup/limits first; use isolated synthetic data and record app/flow versions. Silent partial results are not a pass.
- [ ] Can generate approximately 200 participants.
- [ ] Can generate approximately 1,000 participants.
- [ ] Can generate approximately 5,000 participants.

- [ ] Data covers languages, separate culture offers/interests, optional time zone including blanks, separate participation/validation/openness, typed groups and membership episodes. No required Location or participant group-size field.
- [ ] No real employee data is required. Use isolated fixtures; verify tenant limits/permissions and a supported test-data loading method before large imports.
- [ ] Generators may be optional local repository tooling; deployed workflows stay in existing Microsoft services with no paid runtime.
- [ ] Language one-way, reciprocal and teach-only regression.
- [ ] Culture-only and combined compatibility; interest without sharer is insufficient.
- [ ] Independent participation/validation/open filters and no reactivation by validation.
- [ ] Exact response fields are agreed with #7/#42; admin/system-only data excluded. Comments are generally eligible but not predefined; no Comments notice.
- [ ] Language 2/3 total; Culture/Combined 2–10. Each declared focus has a sharer and different learner; every member participates in at least one; combined supports both collectively.
- [ ] Duplicate requests/acceptance, concurrent last-slot joins, conflicting group-member responses and partial-write retries.
- [ ] Optional blank time zone, all-four-empty save blocking, invalid-focus group suppression and Closed-state preservation after leaving.
- [ ] Empty/invalid/bounded data and required real-tenant integration/access checks.
- [ ] Evidence distinguishes manual synthetic checks from deployed authorization/end-to-end tests.
- [ ] Handles Accepted, Declined and Cancelled requests. Expired state/timers are Later, not MVP acceptance.
- [ ] Repeated execution is prevented or idempotent.
- [ ] Required read access is retained where agreed.
- [ ] Authorization/permission errors are reported under the selected verified approach; no routine admin cleanup or individual manual grants.
- [ ] Request business status is never rolled back due to permission failure.
- [ ] Verify actual permission/connection/licence prerequisites first. Item-specific ACL assignment is an option, not a preselected design.
- [ ] Requester can see own request status and cancel Pending. The personal recipient or any current active target-group member can respond.
- [ ] Unrelated participants cannot read raw requests or act on them by direct access or tampered input.
- [ ] Normal request delivery/response is automatic, without per-person admin grants or routine organiser approval.
- [ ] A failed access operation is visible and recoverable; preserve request history and do not falsely report a usable/successful request.
- [ ] Test response after membership/availability changes and safe retries under the chosen approach.

- [ ] Verify required permissions, settings, connections and existing entitlements before implementation. SharePoint item ACL synchronization is only an option if actually needed and feasible; do not require it by assumption.
- [ ] Through the verified approach, current active members can perform allowed member actions; Left members lose that authority and remaining active members keep it.
- [ ] Exceptional admin support remains available; ordinary joins/leaves require no individual admin grants or manual group maintenance.
- [ ] Retries and partial authorization failures are visible and safe; membership history/business state is not corrupted or falsely reported successful.
- [ ] Test multiple members, departures, stale authorization and direct/tampered invocation. Do not equate app filtering with authorization.
- [ ] Use the selected permitted existing connector/channel and recipient matrix; no preselected email-only or Teams-only decision.
- [ ] Request-received/request-answered and any agreed cancellation/failure events follow that explicit scope.
- [ ] Recipient sees an actionable link without revealing private request/profile information to unrelated users.
- [ ] Routine dispatch requires no organiser emails, individual access grants or paid services.
- [ ] Retry/deduplicate logical events; failed delivery does not roll back accepted requests/memberships.
- [ ] Record agreed failure visibility and exceptional admin handling without creating routine manual work.
- [ ] Tenant delivery tests pass before closure.
- [ ] Only the intended personal recipient or any current active member of the target group may accept/decline; requester can cancel Pending. Reject identity/record tampering.
- [ ] Participants cannot arbitrarily create active membership records.
- [ ] Membership lifecycle changes use the controlled path.
- [ ] Admin can repair records when necessary; no routine admin approval or manual membership maintenance.
- [ ] Enforce controls through the verified supported access method, not UI visibility alone. Do not select a permission architecture before prerequisites are checked.
- [ ] Non-member receives only the approved compatible Discovery projection through the verified path; no general underlying-list access is implied.
- [ ] Any active member can manage Open/Closed/Ended and name/description, and capacity within bounds and never below active member count. Type/focus stay fixed; Ended is final.
- [ ] Non-member cannot change group state.
- [ ] Admin can make necessary exceptional corrections without a routine approval requirement.
- [ ] Verify the access method and its prerequisites before implementation; do not preselect per-item permissions or grant general profile access.
- [ ] #39 — POC-18A: check prerequisites and recommend the simplest supported approach. Access assessment stage; deferred by owner pending ordinary-colleague testing. No working-app changes.
- [ ] #40 — POC-18B: after #39, prove two users automatically access only their own synthetic record in an isolated test.
- [ ] #41 — POC-18C: after #40, integrate and verify private registration before wider colleague testing. Preserve existing data and POC-04 behavior.
- [ ] Define personal-versus-group request type/target field mapping and optional plain-text introduction storage/payload. The suggested 1,000-character limit is not yet approved; review it here.

- [ ] Define group-join send/respond/history/cancel inputs and outputs before package generation. Derive current group/membership/capacity data server-side; caller binding remains with the verified access workstream.
- [ ] No leader/contact role: all current active members see incoming requests and may accept/decline. First valid saved response wins under #47.
- [ ] Define unavailable-target handling without introducing unapproved automatic cancellation.
- [ ] Persist Pending request with trusted participant/group identity; prevent duplicate pending membership requests.
- [ ] Any current active group member can accept/decline; non-members cannot respond; coordinate conflicting responses safely.
- [ ] Recheck group Open state, participant availability, valid focus/member compatibility and capacity at acceptance. Language 2/3 total; Culture/Combined 2–10.
- [ ] Accepted request creates one active membership; slots update automatically.
- [ ] Sender can cancel a Pending request. Declined/Cancelled request preserves history and creates no active membership.
- [ ] Retry and two-users-last-slot scenarios pass #47 tests.
- [ ] No routine admin approval or manual candidate grants; notifications follow #49/#21.
- [ ] Only compatible Open groups with space appear; exclude Ended/Closed/full opportunities.

- [ ] Support Language/Culture/Combined groups, valid distinct sharer/learner relationships for each stated focus and participation in at least one focus. Language capacity 2/3; Culture/Combined 2–10. No participant group-size preference.
- [ ] Show current count/free slots and implement approved #46 group/member display with #7/#42; exclude email/admin/system fields.
- [ ] Current participant and existing-membership treatment follows the approved group rules.
- [ ] Blank optional time zone must not exclude a compatible candidate. Keep supplied time zone catalogue-based; no automatic location derivation or public directory.
- [ ] Use approved authorized data path #42; test real tenant/app behavior before closure.
- [ ] Decide whether the two-group soft warning is wanted and define expectations.
- [ ] Record own acceptance/decision and test evidence before closure.
- [ ] Member can leave without organiser approval; mark membership Left rather than delete history.
- [ ] Ordinary active counts/free slots reflect recorded memberships automatically.

- [ ] Closed stays Closed after departure until an active member reopens it. If remaining members lack the required focus relationships, automatically suppress the group from joinable Discovery without changing stored state.

- [ ] No automatic ending, reopening, replacement assignment, expulsion or rejoin. Remaining members or necessary exceptional admin support can address an invalid-purpose group; no routine recovery approval queue.
- [ ] Setting a participant Inactive does not silently delete memberships; define/document any exceptional follow-up under #6/#13.
- [ ] No automatic return-from-pause rejoin; group-history and waiting derivation remain consistent.
- [ ] Verify repeated departures and actual permission boundaries.
- [ ] Open and Closed can switch or become Ended. Ended is final in MVP; no ordinary reopen-Ended path.
- [ ] Any active member may change allowed group controls and accept/decline join requests; non-members may not. Necessary exceptional admin corrections remain possible.
- [ ] Name/description are editable. Exchange type and language/culture focus stay fixed after creation.
- [ ] Capacity changes remain within Language 2/3 or Culture/Combined 2–10 and cannot fall below current active member count.
- [ ] Only Open groups with space and valid focus relationships can appear as joinable. Open may be full; Closed may have space. Neither then accepts a join.
- [ ] Normal counts/slots update automatically. Leaving does not reopen Closed or automatically end a group; #14 controls departure history and invalid-focus suppression.
- [ ] Personal participation/openness does not silently change group state or remove memberships.
- [ ] Verify caller authority, history and actual tenant behavior; no routine approval or manual count maintenance.
- [ ] Groups stores name, Language/Culture/Combined type, structured language/culture focus, capacity, Open/Closed/Ended state and optional description.
- [ ] Group Members stores group/participant links and Active/Left membership episodes with the agreed timestamps/history mapping. Profiles do not contain manually maintained group text.
- [ ] Language capacity is 2 or 3 total; Culture and Combined capacity is 2–10 total. No participant group-size preference.

- [ ] Each stated language/culture focus has a relevant sharer and a different learner. Every member participates in at least one focus. Combined groups collectively support both focuses; an individual may participate in either or both. Reciprocity is optional.
- [ ] Accepted participants receive authoritative active memberships exactly once. Publish a group only after its required memberships are successfully saved.
- [ ] Initial state is Open if space remains, otherwise Closed. Counts/free slots derive automatically from Active membership rows; do not assume native cross-list calculated columns.
- [ ] Apply #47 protection across all acceptance paths: no duplicate group/member result, over-capacity success or false Accepted state after partial failure.
- [ ] Verify actual list/field names, supported connections/permissions and setup before changing the tenant; no paid service or routine admin group creation.
- [ ] Finalize response input/output contract and unavailable-target handling before the affected package/app wiring. Keep existing approved user-visible request states and eligibility rechecks.
- [ ] Coordinate minimum capacity/retry/recovery safeguards with #47; no full transaction/lock platform or guaranteed automatic recovery of every failure is approved.
- [ ] Only intended recipient/authorized actor can accept or decline; sender sees result.

- [ ] Recheck caller authority, compatibility, availability and applicable capacity at acceptance, rather than trust stale discovery results. For a group join, any current active member may respond; non-members may not.
- [ ] Acceptance creates/updates required group/memberships through one coordinated path.
- [ ] Repeated/concurrent acceptance produces one logical result; failures cannot falsely report completed membership. Use #47 evidence.
- [ ] Decline/cancellation preserves terminal history and creates no active memberships; an accept/cancel race has one consistent winning result under #47.
- [ ] Ordinary path automatic; exceptional repair can use admins.
- [ ] Selected notifications follow #49/#21 without undoing business state on delivery failure.

- [ ] Specify send/history/cancel request fields and flow interfaces before the affected package; distinguish personal recipient from group target with #17. Inputs reference records, not proof of caller identity.
- [ ] Define readable unavailable-target behavior; no automatic cancellation policy approved. Keep acceptance eligibility checks.

- [ ] Review actual TandemMyRequests work: retain if complete/small adjustment, otherwise generate a fresh package. Basic truthful failure responses now; detailed wording/paging at the reader implementation gate.
- [ ] Request from compatible candidate is persisted Pending with trusted requester/recipient identity.
- [ ] Prevent duplicate Pending requests for the same person/group connection; preserve terminal history.
- [ ] Sender can see relevant Pending/Accepted/Declined/Cancelled state; meet-first/expiry/bulk are Later.

- [ ] Sender can cancel while Pending; a later accept cannot create a membership. Recheck availability at acceptance. Decide how pending requests display an unavailable recipient before enabling any automatic cancellation; no new timer/cancellation policy is implied. Notifications follow #49.
- [ ] No routine admin approvals or manual matching; necessary exceptional repair is allowed.
- [ ] Reject tampered identities/recipients and test permission boundaries.
- [ ] No group/membership created until acceptance succeeds.
- [ ] No unhosted Python runtime, external service, premium connector or new hosting/licence dependency.
- [ ] Separate trusted SharePoint normalization, compatibility/status rules and approved response projection.
- [ ] UI controls invoke the flow without duplicating eligibility logic.
- [ ] Reuse culture/language compatibility for #16 without a second matching engine.
- [ ] Run synthetic and tenant cases, including #25; record deployment/export evidence.
- [ ] Caller identity and candidate access satisfy the agreed boundary; do not equate app filtering with authorization.
- [ ] Ranking policy/weights and expectations are unapproved; MVP keeps predictable ordering.
- [ ] Record own acceptance/decision and test evidence before closure.
- [ ] Preserve self exclusion, one-way/reciprocal language fit and teach-only support.
- [ ] Add culture-share/interest compatibility and culture-only/combined scenarios; interest-only cultures do not prove sharing expertise.
- [ ] Gate on independent validation, participation and open-to-connections rules from #46/#6.
- [ ] Optional filters narrow compatible results; do not expose all available profiles as a directory.
- [ ] Implement approved #46 person/group display with #42; exclude email/raw identity/admin/system data and include approved Comments/optional profile fields.
- [ ] Blank optional Time zone does not exclude or invalidate compatible participants; no inferred UTC/location requirement.
- [ ] Implement in Power Automate with existing entitlements, trusted caller/data normalization, bounded queries and approved Power Apps response.
- [ ] No automatic assignments/memberships or routine approvals/per-candidate grants.
- [ ] Record real-data/app integration and tests before closure.
- [ ] Participant can choose Active/Paused/Inactive and open-to-new-connections under the agreed field contract.
- [ ] New self-registration defaults to participation Active and open-to-new-connections Yes; edits/revalidation preserve chosen values.
- [ ] Validation success/failure never overwrites the user's paused/inactive choice.
- [ ] Keep migration confirmation independent; decide discoverability in #48 before exposing migrated data.
- [ ] Derive Waiting/In a group from authoritative memberships, not manual participant labels.

- [ ] Personal openness and group Open/Closed/Ended remain independent. Do not reset group state, delete memberships or rejoin people when personal participation changes. Coordinate eligibility and unavailable-recipient handling with #7/#10.
- [ ] Paused/inactive/closed-to-new-connections profiles do not appear in new discovery; existing history is preserved.
- [ ] Admin can make necessary exceptional corrections, such as departure from company.
- [ ] Retest culture-only and language-only create/edit; no routine admin approvals.
- [ ] Create Culture catalogue with agreed labels/keys and active values; add optional multi-value ShareCultures and LearnCultures lookups.
- [ ] Support language-only, culture-only, share-only and combined profiles. At least one of the four offer/interest fields is needed; all empty blocks form save with useful feedback.
- [ ] Preserve required unique signed-in Participant account. Time zone is OPTIONAL; blank must save and must not invalidate or exclude the profile. Keep existing catalogue lookup.
